title: Phase 1 — cut the Go dependency: ticfac talks to ticks through tk
description:
REWRITTEN 2026-08-27 after Peter asked why ticfac needs Go dependencies at all when it could just run the tk CLI in the sandboxes it already runs. He was right; the first draft of this epic was wrong.

WHAT THE FIRST DRAFT GOT WRONG: it counted ~50 import edges into internal/ and concluded ~50 things needed promoting to a public Go API. Counting what those edges actually DO tells a different story. The tracker touch is FIVE symbols (tick.NewStore, tick.Tick, tick.TypeEpic, tick.TypeTask, tick.StatusOpen) and it lives in the thin cmd/tk/cmd/cloud*.go wrappers, not in the factory packages. The 11 ticksrc edges are the credentials file (Phase 3 splits it anyway). The 3 operator edges are operator.Pending used as a WIRE TYPE in dashboard/client.go:121,168 — a JSON field, never a tracker call. The rest are one-offs.

THE APPROACH: ticfac reaches ticks through `tk ... --json`. 36 tk commands support it and the types are generated from schemas/ via make codegen-go/codegen-ts, so it is a maintained contract, not scraped output.

THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT IS CONSISTENCY. cloud/sandbox/required-tk-commands already declares the tk subcommands the container must have, and the image's last Dockerfile layer install-checks each one. The container has never imported Go — it shells out. Having the container shell out while the laptop imports Go is two answers to one question.

WHAT IT AVOIDS: promoting a package out of internal/ is a permanent promise — rename a function afterwards and you break a downstream consumer. The old Phase 1 would have forced a decision about which internals of ticks become a frozen surface, to serve exactly one consumer. The CLI is already that surface.

THE WORK:
1. Repoint the five tracker symbols at `tk ... --json` calls.
2. Give the factory dashboard its own wire struct instead of borrowing operator.Pending.
3. Move dashboard.DefaultHarnessBytes so cmd/tk/cmd/root.go:13 stops importing internal/factory/dashboard.
4. Resolve the one-offs: internal/styles (TUI theme — ticfac gets its own; do not bind two products' visual identity), internal/github (device flow — duplicate it or shell to gh; do NOT promote, it handles token exchange and a frozen public API around credentials is a liability), internal/herd/gitcmd and internal/herd/collect (git helpers — own copy or a tk equivalent, decide per call site), internal/herd/dashboard (one reference whose import comment says it is deliberate — check it survives at all once ticfac owns its dashboard).
5. Publish the required-command list and add a test that FAILS when ticks removes or renames one of them.

PERFORMANCE, checked rather than assumed: shelling out costs a process launch per call, and the hot path is fine. internal/factory/dashboard/model.go:21 refreshes every 2s and reads the FACTORY'S HTTP API, not the local tracker; cost telemetry is 30s; the 1s display tick reads nothing. No tk invocation sits in a render loop. Rule for this epic: if a call site needs many ticks, use one batched --json call rather than a loop of small ones. If a real hot path appears later, revisit with a measurement — not in advance.

NOTHING MOVES IN THIS EPIC. The factory stays in this repo and simply stops importing ticks.
acceptance_criteria: Nothing under cloud/factory or internal/factory imports a ticks internal/ package THAT STAYS IN TICKS. Two edges are expected to survive and are not violations: internal/ticksrc (deferred to Phase 3, which splits the credentials file with a migration) and internal/gatewaytrace + internal/cloud/state (the factory's OWN packages — the spec's What-moves table lists them as moving to ticfac, so the edge is internal-to-ticfac and survives the move by design). NO package has been promoted out of internal/ — the diff adds no new public Go surface. cmd/tk/cmd/root.go does not import internal/factory/dashboard. A committed required-tk-commands list for the factory exists, with a test that fails if a listed command or flag is removed or renamed. go test ./... green.
closed_reason: Completed: the factory no longer imports ticks. Tracker reads go through tk --json behind one batched helper; the dashboard has its own wire struct; four one-off borrowings are copies with stated reasons; root.go is factory-free. Ships a derived required-tk-commands list with a sabotage-proven guard, pinned exit codes across all three tk outcomes, and a measurement of what factory code costs a tk build. NOTHING was promoted out of internal/ — the phase left ticks unchanged, which was its thesis. PR #68 merged with a green CI gate.
